video_title: Adam Silver's BIG Presser & Tradeability Odds | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: why hockey is a more physical sport than basketball
quotes.excerpt: Hockey is one of the most physical sports out there. You have to do everything you would do
quotes.quote: Hockey is one of the most physical sports out there. You have to do everything you would do while playing a normal team sport game, except you have to do it backward often and on skates. One of the funniest things when I started covering hockey when I was much younger, I would hear people say, 'He's a good player, but he can't skate.' And I would be like, 'I'm pretty sure he's skating out there.' That seems like skating. And they're like, 'No, no, no, no. There's a big difference between skating at an NHL level and not.' It's not even just doing it all on skates, it's doing it at a certain level on skates.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: concerns about the Portland Trail Blazers' front office management
quotes.excerpt: It's not just what happened with the Lakers and the Mark Walter situation. It's what's going on in Portland.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I would ask Adam about how they vet potential owners and whether the events of the last year have made them rethink a stronger process. Because it's not just what happened with the Lakers and the Mark Walter situation. It's what's going on in Portland. You are talking about a battle between the team and its city. You have fans in fear of their team being taken away, you have employees being fired right and left. It is hard to argue that the Portland Trail Blazers, having fired medical staff, travel people, long-time broadcasters who know the game and the history of the team, it's hard to argue they're better off now than they were before Tom Dunden took over as owner.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: It's tough to change now because the cost of these teams are astronomical. Gone are the days when Jerry Buss could buy the Lakers for 200 million and own it as a family asset for decades to come, or even Mark Cuban decades later buying the team for a relatively reasonable price, a bargain in today's numbers, and buy it with the intention of owning the team for decades to come. Nowadays, a lot of these new owners are looking at these teams like assets. We've got this asset and we can buff it up and wait for the new TV deal to come in five, six years, whenever that may be, and we can flip it and make a billion dollars on our five-year investment.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA teams are public trusts, not just assets for billionaires
quotes.excerpt: Sports teams are a public trust. They just are. You don't own them, you take care of them.
quotes.quote: Sports teams are a public trust. They just are. You don't own them, you take care of them until the next owner. The NBA gets to decide whether that's the case or not. The sports leagues. So I'll give you an example. I live in a neighborhood where for some of the houses in the neighborhood, the HOA says that you can't build a second story onto your house because there's a great view and it would block the view for the rest of the entire neighborhood. That's the rule. And you know that's the rule when you decide to buy the property. Property values for those houses are lower than they would be for elsewhere in the neighborhood because you can't build a second story onto the house. On the other hand, they get first shot at this great view. That's why the second story is important in that house. You can make rules that affect what these teams go for and who buys them. They could decide, these are the things that we need an NBA owner to do, including, I'm not going to move the team for 15 years. I've got to sign that, and so I can get indentured into the system. You can make decisions that hedge funds aren't in. They only recently decided to let them in.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: the Clippers' front office is currently leaderless and in chaos
quotes.excerpt: I had a source that is plugged into the Clippers. This person told me that in the front office
quotes.quote: I had a source that is plugged into the Clippers. This person told me that in the front office right now, they were leaderless. It was a rudderless ship at the moment, which is not all that surprising because the three top people in basketball operations are gone. The assumption is that Trent Redden will take over the day-to-day operations of the team, but right now it's chaos over there as they're trying to figure out who's calling the shots, who's the ultimate decision-maker, and who can sign off on this Kawhi Leonard deal.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry's trade odds are low despite the Warriors' struggles
quotes.excerpt: Steph Curry is currently entering the last year of his contract. I've got the odds of Steph Curry
quotes.quote: Steph Curry is currently entering the last year of his contract. I've got the odds of Steph Curry being traded at 20 to 1. I don't think as much as Joe Lacob has been talking about planning for the future in a way that is driving Warriors fans and me, frankly, absolutely crazy when you have Steph Curry right now, he's not going to be the guy who traded Steph Curry. I think that if they decide to end their partnership, it will be because they can't agree to a new extension and that he will go off in the summer to great fanfare, but I don't even think that's going to happen.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry's father is a huge asset for his career longevity
quotes.excerpt: I think that Steph is so smart about the way he goes about his business.
quotes.quote: I think that Steph is so smart about the way he goes about his business. I think he has the example of his father. I think that's a huge asset when you're trying to figure out the end of your career. You can talk to your dad who already went through it, and you also watched him go through it to an extent. And I think he knows that when his time is done, and that is sooner rather than later, and his career is sort of quantified and looked back on, he has so many championships. And the fact that he could be a guy who stayed with a franchise from the beginning to the end, which he has said multiple times is important to him, is something that he is going to be able to lean on for the next 50 years.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Bryant's request to be traded on the radio
quotes.excerpt: Kobe asked to be traded on the radio. So there's no there's no controversy of, oh, you're just
quotes.quote: Kobe asked to be traded on the radio. So there's no there's no controversy of, oh, you're just saying that or he said or that why was the source. Kobe asked to be traded on the radio. But I will say this, and I knew Kobe very, very well and covered him almost from the time he got to the NBA, is that while that was true, and that came from what you're talking about right now with Steph, doesn't he have this desire to just go somewhere he can win? In the end, it was extremely important and meaningful to Kobe that he finished with the Lakers. That was something in the last year of him playing, year and a half, two years of him playing, is something he talked to me about.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: why Kyrie Irving is unlikely to publicly demand a trade
quotes.excerpt: I don't think Kyrie is going to really publicly make a big stink and ask out.
quotes.quote: I don't think Kyrie is going to really publicly make a big stink and ask out. That's just he's talked to me so many times about being happy in Dallas, feeling like the organization is behind him in a way that, frankly, he didn't feel that way at his previous stops. And he's tired. It's been a long time, I'm tired of it. I don't know what spurred that. I assume there must have been some incident with his family, right? Because that's normally where where players just sort of draw the line. I don't think he wants to go to LA to be paired with Luka Doncic. That's way more, you know, when you think about a where would he go that he would okay the trade or want the trade or not? Like, where would he go where he would get less of that kind of stuff?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic's status as an untouchable superstar
quotes.excerpt: Nikola Jokic, Denver Nuggets, Uber star, not a superstar, Uber star, multi-time MVP, NBA champion.
quotes.quote: Nikola Jokic, Denver Nuggets, Uber star, not a superstar, Uber star, multi-time MVP, NBA champion, still very much in the prime of his career, still putting up the kind of numbers that make you wonder why he's not a six-time MVP, is on the last year of his contract and is on a team that continues to erode. Now, it would take some great fruits, Rachel. It would take some great fruits for the front office in Denver to trade Nikola Jokic. But he would also return, I feel like we always say this about the biggest package in NBA history, but like it would be a pretty big trade package that he would get back.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: why the Nuggets are unlikely to trade Nikola Jokic
quotes.excerpt: I would put them a little lower because of recent statements that Rich Paul has made.
quotes.quote: I would put them a little lower because of recent statements that Rich Paul has made. Rich Paul basically came out and said, and I don't have it in front of me, so please correct me if I have the timeline wrong, but he said that we've agreed to have him play the first few months of the season, a couple months, three months of the season and see where we are after that for contract talks. So obviously, in the summer and even prior to that, Rich Paul had been pounding and pounding, I need to get him an extension, Anthony needs an extension, he should only be traded to teams that will give him an extension, all of that kind of stuff. Clearly, that didn't go anywhere and you don't have as much leverage in the summer because an unhappy player doesn't mean as much in the summer, right? A guy in the season who makes life difficult for the front office and the coaching staff and suddenly has, 'Oh no, my back doesn't feel that well,' all of that stuff, players have ways to force the situation to a head. You just don't have that in the summer.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's potential trade destination and player option decision
quotes.excerpt: the old player option on James Harden, which he'll probably opt out of and get two more years

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Trade kicker, finally your player option, the old player option on James Harden, which he'll probably opt out of and get two more years in the back end with some team. Greatest businessman in the NBA history.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Atlanta as a potential trade destination for James Harden
quotes.excerpt: I think Atlanta is another team that's a piece away from maybe being really good

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Atlanta. Atlanta. Like I look at that roster.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: Tim Bontemps. You think Tim Bontemps is going to trade for James Harden?

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: It's a good point. I didn't think of Tim Bontemps down there. I look, I think Atlanta is another team that's a piece away from maybe being really good.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating CJ McCollum's performance and age-related decline
quotes.excerpt: it seemed like his age caught up with him in the second half of games
quotes.quote: CJ McCollum had a great run with them, but I look at him in the playoffs and he was the best player they had in the playoffs, but it seemed like his age caught up with him in the second half of games if my memory serves me correctly with that. He's also mid-30s, so he's not a long-term answer there.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Proposed trade package for James Harden involving CJ McCollum and Aaron Wiggins
quotes.excerpt: CJ McCollum just acquired Aaron Wiggins, maybe you put him in that deal, you get James Harden
quotes.quote: CJ McCollum just acquired Aaron Wiggins, maybe you put him in that deal, you get James Harden, and you roll the dice that Harden can be the kind of dynamic table-setting guard that I think they need. They don't have a lot of shot creators down there. I mean Jalen Johnson is one. Jalen Johnson is a stud. And look, Jalen Johnson and Trey Young, the brief times that they played together, at least a couple years ago, they look like they had some chemistry there on that pick and roll.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Questioning the logic of trading for James Harden over CJ McCollum
quotes.excerpt: if you're worried that CJ McCollum in his 30s runs out of gas at the end of games
quotes.quote: If you're worried that CJ McCollum in his 30s runs out of gas at the end of games, are you trading for James Harden who's three years older?

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial and competitive reality of James Harden's contract
quotes.excerpt: it's 30 million eating out of your books for three years. He's 37 now
quotes.quote: It's 30 million eating out of your books for three years. He's 37 now. And he is a workhorse, he has put his body on the line for his teams. I mean if you look at his games played in regular seasons, it's remarkable. And you made the point that they need to try to sit him down and rest him more this year, whether he likes it or not, so he can be more, more have that gas for the playoffs. But still, I just don't think that you're a team. I think that Cleveland had to give him the money because they took a gamble on putting the team together that they did, they obviously were done with Darius Garland. It didn't work, right?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Aaron Wiggins' potential as an improved player in Atlanta
quotes.excerpt: I actually think Wiggins is going to be one of the most improved players in the NBA
quotes.quote: I actually think Wiggins is going to be one of the most improved players in the NBA. I do. I think giving him a broader role in Atlanta, maybe it's not exactly Nikhil Alexander-Walker when he left, but Aaron Wiggins was light years better than what he showed or what the opportunities he got in Oklahoma City. That guy can play. I actually think he might be more impactful than Lou Dort with that team because I think he's a little bit more diverse.
